publicationIncident.what: publishing snapshot 61 replaced the product's current publication (14) by a new one (15) for about 90 seconds
publicationIncident.cause: POST /platform/publication/publish is a product-wide release: DataPlanePublicationWriter makes EVERY REVIEW_REQUIRED dataset snapshot of the product a member and flips them all to PUBLISHED, and the new publication supersedes the previous one. The request names one snapshot; the operation releases all.

effect.sweptIn: 58 and 59 (the wrong model - I had written they must never be published), 57 and 60 (earlier test loads), and 53 (dataset version 73, 225 resources) - a pending candidate that was NOT mine

publicationIncident.remedy: POST /platform/publication/rollback to publication 14 - status ROLLED_BACK; publication 14 is current again
publicationIncident.residueTheApiCannotUndo: dataset snapshots 53, 57, 58, 59, 60, 61 keep status PUBLISHED although they are not members of the current publication. Snapshot 53 can no longer be released through the normal flow by whoever prepared it.
publicationIncident.lesson: on a shared product, never call publish to demonstrate one dataset. A governed load into a product creates a REVIEW_REQUIRED snapshot that the next product release will sweep in.
